newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.9 pct in March - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.9 pct in March - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.9 percent in the third week of fiscal March versus February, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 8.4 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 8.6 percent in the week ended March 22 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Despite robust numbers, the business picture was mixed, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"The numbers look good, but a couple of the retailers told me that they're a little disappointed in the way the week turned out," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Both national and regional department stores indicated that sales momentum had slowed, and their year-over-year gains fell noticeably from the previous week's levels, he said.
"But nevertheless it's nothing to be ashamed of," Eilenberg said, adding that retailers, especially the discount stores, should not expect a pending slowdown.
In merchandise categories, seasonal hard-lines accounted for much of the strength at discount stores, while apparel consistently outperformed home-goods at department stores, he said.
Looking at sales for March overall, Eilenberg said that Easter sales will probably help stores achieve their monthly targets.
